page: Microsoft Azure E192ids_v6 is an isolated memory-optimized virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. Powered by the Intel Xeon 8573C processor based on the x86_64 architecture, the server runs at 4.2 GHz across 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated vCPUs with simultaneous multithreading. Memory and cache layout includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB shared L3 cache. The CPU instruction set features hardware support for AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8, optimizing compute-dense matrix and vector calculations.

System memory totals 1832.0 GB, providing an allocation of 9.54 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled with 11340 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity, alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage. Hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs are not present. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate top-decile multi-core computing, highlighted by a multi-core stress-ng result of 158923.19, Geekbench multi-core score of 21589.0, and high memory bandwidth reaching 430.1 GB/sec on uncached reads. Real-world application benchmarks verify this scale, delivering 179.31 million Redis SET operations per second and high-throughput static web serving.

The hardware configuration trades single-threaded optimization for aggregate multi-core and memory scalability. Single-core stress-ng performance places in the median percentile, whereas parallel throughput and cache-coherent operations sit in the top tier. Qualitatively, consolidating high vCPU counts, vast RAM capacity, and extensive local NVMe scratch storage into an isolated single node delivers high infrastructure efficiency for enterprise architectures. E192ids_v6 is best matched for memory-resident databases, real-time caching deployments, distributed data processing, and large transactional database engines.
description: Microsoft Azure E192ids_v6 is an isolated memory-optimized instance featuring 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V, the platform provides 1832.0 GB of memory, translating to 9.54 GB per vCPU, and is bundled with 11340 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The processor incorporates AVX-512 and Intel AMX instruction sets, contributing to top-tier multi-threaded compute performance and 430.1 GB/sec of uncached memory read bandwidth. Although single-threaded CPU benchmarks reflect moderate performance, aggregate multi-core throughput and memory capacity are in the top tier, yielding over 179 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking discrete GPUs, the configuration maximizes resource density for CPU- and memory-heavy workloads. The instance is suited for enterprise relational databases, large in-memory caching systems, transactional engines, and large-scale data analytics pipelines.
